advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse the already-fetched `ticket` state in show_ticket by calling the pure `cross_session_warning(state, ...)` instead of re-reading via `_cross_session`/`cross_session_warning_for`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py:39: `state = show_ticket(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` — cross_session_warning_for re-fetches the same state the reader already holds
src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py:24-27: the pure detector reads only `claimed_session`/`claim_harness` from state, both present on the already-fetched `ticket`
advisory.finding: show_ticket (read path) fetches the full compiled ticket via rebar.show_ticket(...) and then calls _cross_session(ticket_id), which re-reads the SAME ticket (another show_ticket) plus load_config inside cross_session_warning_for — a redundant second store read when the already-fetched `ticket` dict already contains claimed_session and claim_harness that the pure cross_session_warning(state, ...) detector consumes.
scenarios: Every MCP show_ticket call incurs a duplicate ticket read plus a config load solely to compute the advisory.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the reopen test comment to match what it does, and add coverage that exercises reopen_ticket attaching a NON-null cross_session_warning key (a held-then-reopened ticket).
evidence: tests/unit/test_cross_session_mcp.py comment: `# A closed ticket has no live claim, so it does NOT warn; re-claim to hold it, then reopen.` — no re-claim is actually done before `out = _write_tools()["reopen_ticket"](tid)`
assertion `assert out.get("cross_session_warning") is None` passes due to the cleared claim, contradicting the 'happy path (implementer sees)' framing of a warning-carrying reopen
advisory.finding: test_reopen_warns_for_other_session has a docstring/comment describing a re-claim step it never performs, making the test's intent misleading; the assertion (cross_session_warning is None) is correct only because a closed ticket has no live claim, not because of any re-claim.
scenarios: A reader trusting the comment believes the additive key is exercised in its non-null form for reopen, but no test asserts reopen ever emits a non-null warning.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an MCP-surface best-effort test: monkeypatch cross_session_warning_for to raise, then assert comment_ticket/show_ticket (and a raw-dict transition) still succeed with cross_session_warning None/absent.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:44 `try:` / `return cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=None)` / `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — the advisory must never fail a real operation` / `return None`
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py added `_cross_session` with identical `except Exception: return None` swallow

ABSENCE: test_cross_session_mcp.py has no monkeypatch of cross_session_warning_for to raise, unlike the CLI equivalent test_cross_session_cli.py:162 `test_warning_is_best_effort_on_detector_error` which patches `cross_session.cross_session_warning_for = _boom` and asserts rc==0 and the mutation landed
advisory.finding: The newly added best-effort swallow-and-degrade wrappers `_cross_session` in _mcp_writes.py and _mcp_reads.py (try/except Exception -> return None, with the stated contract 'the advisory must never fail a real operation') have no test. No test in test_cross_session_mcp.py injects a failure into cross_session_warning_for to verify the MCP write/read still succeeds (mutation lands, response validates, no warning) when the advisory compute raises. If the except clause were removed or narrowed, every single-ticket MCP write/show would start propagating advisory-compute failures and no MCP test would catch it.
scenarios: cross_session_warning_for raises (corrupt/locked/absent state read) while comment_ticket or show_ticket runs as a different session
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that does `monkeypatch.setattr(rebar._mcp_writes, 'cross_session_warning_for', _boom)` (and the reads module), invokes comment_ticket/show_ticket/transition_ticket as sess-B, and asserts the mutation landed and cross_session_warning is None/absent.
